title: Swarm Chemistry (new class, heterogeneous self-propelled agents): from a uniform random mix, one species forms tight wandering clusters and the other a halo around each (blue density 3x background at ~3 core radii, 0 inside)
summary: New class: Sayama's Swarm Chemistry, boids whose species differ only in kinetic recipe (neighbour radius, speeds, cohesion, alignment, separation, random steering, pace keeping), all agents responding to all others in range. A screen of 60 random two-species recipes (240 agents, 600 steps; screen_seed2_60recipes.txt) mostly gives species-pure clusters or domain-wide bands; recipe 2/23 (world.py, 480 agents on a periodic 848^2 box from a uniform random start) gives 5-12 dense red clusters at a time, each wrapped in a loose halo of the faster, longer-ranged blue species (v23_N480.png). Around red-cluster centres the blue density is 0 out to ~2 mean red radii, peaks at 3.2x its mean density at ~3 radii and returns to the mean by ~6 (prof23.png, track23.py); labkit (pack_seed1) finds 11 persistent clusters moving up to 7.5 body lengths but merges outnumber splits 12 to 1. No claims: the halo is a quasi-equilibrium arrangement of a second species, not tested for work, and there is no division yet.
